title: Budgets, alerts, quotas and spending limits

videos.script: A budget does not stop spending. That is the first thing to know about it, and the thing people least expect. {{nostop}} A budget is an amount and a few thresholds. When spending crosses one, Google sends a message. The machines keep running. {{thresholds}} Some thresholds look at money already spent. Others look at a forecast, and can warn you on the fifth day of the month. {{forecast}} The message can go to a person, by e-mail. Or to a Pub/Sub topic, where a program reads it at once. {{pubsub}} That part your lab can run. The emulator delivers three moments of an invented month, and a short program decides what to do with each. {{program}} Past the budget, a program could switch billing off. Everything would stop, and some data could be deleted. That is the price of a cap. {{cap}} So the finer tool is a quota. Lower it on the API that charges per call, and a runaway bug is refused instead of billed. {{end}}
